source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of the exact UTF-8 <verse ...>...</verse> substring, including markup, whitespace, written forms, and any reading notes. No XML reserialization or Hebrew normalization.
source.public_versification_note: English Genesis 31:55 is bound to Hebrew Gen 32:1, whose original XML record includes the note KJV:Gen.31.55.

key_decisions.decision: Render the idiom ten counts as ten times, possibly a round number, and preserve Jacob’s accusation and protective attribution.
Keep dream, mating action, and three markings; do not merge this divine explanation into chapter 30’s branch technique.
Retain source wording God of Bethel, both remembered actions, urgent commands, and birthplace; do not harmonize it to the wording of 28:13.
Preserve the daughters’ accusations of being treated as outsiders, sold, and deprived of the proceeds; do not endorse Laban’s ownership claim.
Keep Rachel’s theft explicit and render teraphim as household gods without supplying motive or inheritance theory.
Preserve the source’s theft-of-the-heart wordplay alongside Rachel’s literal theft; use stole away for covert departure.
Preserve the uncertain good-to-bad idiom as a prohibition on formal pronouncement, since Laban still speaks extensively.
Retain Laban’s accusation and violent captive image as his rhetoric; identify daughters without accepting his possessive claim.
Render sons as grandchildren because the group includes Jacob’s children, including Dinah; preserve daughters and rebuke.
Keep Laban’s threat and repeat the uncertain divine warning consistently with verse 24.
Keep Jacob’s severe unwitting oath, public search permission, and narrator’s disclosure; do not claim this caused Rachel’s later death.
Render the way-of-women idiom plainly as menstruation and preserve Rachel’s deferential address and successful concealment.
Render the bearing-of-loss verb as absorbing liability and preserve Laban’s day/night repayment demand.
Retain the distinctive divine title Fear of Isaac and legal force of rebuke/decide; keep suffering and labor as what God saw.
Preserve Laban’s sweeping ownership claims as speech, including women, children, animals, and property; do not validate them narratively.
Retain both Aramaic and Hebrew-related names, whose shared witness-heap meaning is explained in vocabulary.
Preserve watch/watchpost wordplay and mutual absence; do not recast this wary boundary as a sentimental blessing.
Keep the warning against affliction and additional wives, human absence, and divine witness; leave Laban’s inconsistency visible.
Preserve reciprocal boundary and explicit harmful purpose; do not claim an absolute ban on all future crossing.
Reflect the plural Hebrew judge and Laban’s polytheistic formulation while distinguishing Jacob’s oath by the Fear of Isaac.
Map public 31:55 to Hebrew 32:1, including its embedded English-versification note; render sons as grandchildren because these are Jacob’s children.
